title: MOQ Values Matter — Conceptual Model
description: Conceptual schema defining the project's architecture: entity types, relationships, and constraints. This is a type-level model — it does not enumerate specific instances of laws, glossary entries, or Atlas entries. Instances live in the project's MDX files.
scope: Architectural skeleton. Stable across instance changes. Updated only when the project's underlying conceptual structure shifts.

foundationalAxioms.description: Non-negotiable foundational claims grounding the entire model. These are not derived from other elements; they ground the rest.

axioms.statement: Value is the primary organising principle of reality, prior to subject-object division.
Reality consists of static value patterns and Dynamic Quality.
Static value patterns operate at four levels in moral hierarchy: Physical, Biological, Social, Intellectual.
Higher levels have moral precedence over lower levels but depend on them for substrate.
Dynamic Quality cannot be defined, operationalised, or systematised. It is the pre-conceptual source of novelty, recognisable only after stabilisation into static patterns.
Stories, narratives, myths, and symbolic meaning are always social-level patterns, never intellectual-level patterns.

ontology.description: Type definitions for entities in the project. Each entity type defines what kind of thing it is, its required properties, and its constraints.

Quality.definition: The primary reality from which subjects and objects arise. Pre-intellectual, recognisable but not fully definable.

DynamicQuality.definition: The pre-conceptual source of novelty, change, and moral progress.
constraints: May only be referenced as the pre-conceptual source
Recognisable only after passing into static patterns
Not equivalent to creativity, exploration, or novelty as behaviours
Cannot be the mechanism through which any process operates
DynamicQuality.rationale: AX-05 — most easily violated constraint in the project; requires active guarding.

StaticPattern.definition: Stabilised forms of value that emerge from Dynamic Quality and persist over time.
StaticPattern.scope: Operates at one of four MOQ levels
constraints: Must be located at exactly one primary MOQ level
Quality is partially constituted by structural conformance, not separate from it

Level.definition: One of four ordered levels at which static value patterns operate.

properties.conditionalPrecedence: Precedence applies when lower-level patterns are functioning; intellectual precedence over social applies only when intellectual patterns meet their structural conditions

Biological.mode: Active resistance to entropy through self-maintenance

Intellectual.mode: Symbolic operation maintaining quality through structural conditions
Intellectual.precedenceConditional: Earned through meeting intellectual structural conditions; not automatic

crossLevelRules: Higher levels cannot originate lower-level patterns — they cannot bring into existence what the lower level has not produced as substrate
Higher levels can stabilise, constrain, formalise, distort, or modulate lower-level patterns — this is legitimate cross-level interaction, not a hierarchy violation

Lower levels enable higher levels by providing substrate, but do not produce them — biological cooperation does not create social patterns by itself; social organisation does not create intellectual patterns by itself
Reductionism across levels is prohibited — a higher level cannot be explained as merely a configuration of the lower level it depends on
What is high quality at one level is not necessarily high quality at another level, and may be the opposite — quality is level-relative even though the levels exist in holistic relation

Law.definition: A structural axis describing a condition that any system at the relevant level must satisfy. Laws define the dimensional space within which value patterns are evaluated.

properties.title: string
properties.structuralFunction: string — what the axis does at its level
properties.failureMode: string — how the structural mechanism breaks down
properties.atlasCoordination: list of AtlasEntry references with relationship notes
properties.moqPlacement: string — position within the level's law system

constraints: Must pass the universe test: would the structural requirement hold for any system at the relevant level regardless of substrate?
Must describe structural conditions, not human social patterns specifically
Must not invoke Dynamic Quality as a mechanism
Must not collapse into descriptions of one level from another level's perspective
Must distinguish description from prescription

universeTest.statement: A candidate law passes if its structural requirement would hold for any system at its level — biological, social, intellectual, or physical — regardless of evolutionary path, substrate, species, or implementation.
universeTest.rationale: Distinguishes structural requirements from descriptions of human-specific or earth-specific phenomena.

AtlasEntry.definition: A specific value pattern located within the dimensional space defined by the Laws.
AtlasEntry.scope: Has exactly one primary Level; operates as a position within the structural axes at and across levels

properties.title: string
properties.tenSectionStructure: ordered structure with all 10 canonical sections required for Canon status

AtlasEntry.qualityDefinition: An Atlas entry's quality is its profile across the structural axes (Laws), not a single number. A pattern that supports multiple structural axes simultaneously without trade-offs is high quality; a pattern that serves some axes at the cost of others produces specific structural distortions and is lower quality.
constraints: Must follow the 10-section canonical structure for Canon status
Must declare exactly one primary Level (score = 2)
Must include explicit boundary rejections
Must identify failure modes
Must not invoke Dynamic Quality as a mechanism
Score profile must reflect functional role, not importance or moral weight

GlossaryEntry.definition: A deep-linkable atomic definition of a term used across the project.

properties.title: string
properties.relatedAtlas: optional AtlasEntry reference for Tier 2 entries

Tier1.description: Full definition — used for terms that have no Atlas entry. Includes precise functional definition, explicit not-statements establishing context against conventional thinking, and role within the project.

Tier2.description: Thin pointer — short summary plus link to Atlas entry where the full definition lives.
appliesTo: Terms that have full Atlas entries

Layer.definition: Classification indicating the scope and origin of a glossary entry or other element.

MOQ Foundation.description: Pirsig's core concepts; cannot be redefined by this project

Project-Wide.description: Shared vocabulary across the full project, defined by this project

Circle/Ripple Theory.description: Scoped to the supplementary Circle/Ripple Theory only

Status.definition: Current standing of an entry within the project's governance system.

transitions.promotionToCanon: Requires explicit evaluation against the Canon Promotion Checklist and explicit Canon Declaration
transitions.deprecation: Must be explicitly marked; silent removal prohibited

Status.constraint: Status values not in this list are drift errors and must be corrected. The previously used 'Canon-stable' is non-standard and must be replaced with 'Canon'.

ContentType.definition: Machine-readable type field required in every content file's frontmatter.

GovernanceDocument.definition: Documents that define the project's operating rules, constraints, and procedures.

authority.ai-instructions.mdx: Single authoritative file for AI behaviour; governs on conflict
authority.canon-governance.mdx: Defines what Canon is; governs on Canon-status conflicts
authority.supplementary documents: Apply within their stated scope only; defer to authoritative files on conflict

Cluster.definition: A Canon cluster page organising structural relationships between existing Canon Atlas entries.
constraints: References only Canon entries
Introduces no new patterns or evaluative claims
Preserves MOQ hierarchy and boundary discipline
Updated only to maintain accuracy when linked Canon entries change
Justified only when existing Canon entries exhibit a stable, recurring structural relationship that cannot be captured clearly via cross-links alone

LawBelongsToLevel.constraint: Each Law belongs to exactly one Level. Laws within a level form an integrated system; no law operates independently of the others.

AtlasEntryHasPrimaryLevel.constraint: Each Atlas entry has exactly one primary Level (score = 2 in that level's row of the score profile).

AtlasEntryScoresAgainstLaws.description: An Atlas entry has a structural axis profile expressing how it relates to each Law: supports the structural requirement, undermines it, or transforms it.

GlossaryEntryMayPointToAtlasEntry.constraint: Tier 2 glossary entries point to Atlas entries; Tier 1 entries do not.

EntityHasStatus.constraint: Valid status values depend on the entity's ContentType (see Status definition).

EntityHasContentType.constraint: Required field in every content file's frontmatter.

ClusterReferencesAtlasEntries.constraint: Must reference two or more Canon Atlas entries; may not reference Draft or Reviewed entries.

LevelDependsOnLowerLevel.constraint: Each level except Physical depends on the immediately lower level for substrate.

LevelHasMoralPrecedenceOverLowerLevels.constraint: Each level has moral precedence over all lower levels, conditional on the higher level meeting its structural conditions.

qualityArchitecture.description: How the entities work together to constitute the project's quality framework.

dimensionalSpace.concept: Laws define the structural axes; Atlas entries are positions within that dimensional space.
dimensionalSpace.implication: A value pattern's quality is its profile across the structural axes, not a single property of the pattern itself.
dimensionalSpace.evaluation: A pattern that supports multiple structural axes simultaneously without trade-offs is high quality. A pattern that serves some axes at the cost of others produces specific structural distortions and is lower quality.

valueElevation.concept: Higher-quality patterns emerge from honest engagement of high-quality patterns at the same level.
valueElevation.scope: Applies within levels (intellectual synthesis, social emergence) and across levels (level transitions in MOQ).
valueElevation.constraint: Cannot be forced or scheduled; emerges as a property of how high-quality patterns relate, not as a Dynamic Quality intervention.
valueElevation.rationale: Same value-elevation phenomenon that produces MOQ level transitions, occurring within levels among static patterns.

structuralUniversality.concept: The universe test as quality criterion for laws.
structuralUniversality.test: Would the structural requirement hold for any system at its level — biological, social, intellectual, or physical — regardless of evolutionary path, substrate, species, or implementation?
structuralUniversality.implication: If a candidate law fails this test, it describes a human-specific or substrate-specific phenomenon and belongs in the Atlas, not in the Laws.

canonAsIntellectualStaticQuality.concept: Canon entries are the project's own intellectual-level static patterns.
canonAsIntellectualStaticQuality.implication: Canon governance is therefore self-referential: the project applies its own intellectual-level laws to its own knowledge production.
constraints: Coherence: Canon entries must hold together internally (L-I-02)
Correspondence: Canon entries must remain responsive to evidence and argument (L-I-03)
Revisability: Canon retains capacity for warranted update (L-I-04)
Integrity: Canon promotion must respond to epistemic warrants, not social or institutional pressure (L-I-05)
Communication: Canon must be transmissible and testable (L-I-06)

holisticSystemNature.concept: The MOQ hierarchy is a living, emerging, holistic structure — not a one-directional chain of causation. The four levels exist in constant relation to each other, with quality emerging from how patterns at every level interact.
holisticSystemNature.rationale: What Pirsig stated simply: something that is high quality at one level is not necessarily high quality at another level, and may be quite the opposite. But the system is whole. The elements always exist in relation to each other.
implications: The hierarchy describes precedence under conflict, not isolation between levels
Higher levels operate on lower-level substrate continuously — modulating, formalising, stabilising it — without thereby originating it
Lower levels constrain and enable higher levels continuously — without thereby reducing them
Quality emerges from the whole pattern of interaction across levels, not from any single level operating in isolation
Cross-level interaction is essential to how the levels actually function; the hierarchy without interaction would be sterile rather than living
holisticSystemNature.commonMisreading: The MOQ hierarchy is sometimes treated as if it forbade all higher-to-lower influence. This overstates the prohibition. What MOQ forbids is reduction (explaining a higher level as merely a configuration of a lower one) and origination (treating a higher level as the source of a lower-level pattern). What MOQ permits and requires is continuous cross-level interaction — what philosophy of mind sometimes calls 'downward causation' — through which higher levels operate on the substrate they depend on.

qualityIsLevelRelative.principle: What is high quality at one level may be low quality at another level — sometimes the opposite. A biologically high-quality response (immediate aggression to threat) may be socially destructive. A socially high-quality compliance (loyalty to corrupt authority) may be intellectually degrading. A intellectually high-quality challenge (questioning founding assumptions) may be socially destabilising in ways that warrant their own caution.
qualityIsLevelRelative.implication: Atlas entries must therefore be evaluated across all levels, not just the level of their primary placement. A pattern's full quality profile is its score across the structural axes at every level it interacts with — primary, secondary, and constraint.

boundaryConstraints.description: Constraints that prevent category errors and protect the project's coherence.

dynamicQualityProtection.rule: Dynamic Quality cannot be defined, operationalised, modularised, treated as a method, framework, lens, mechanism, or driver.
dynamicQualityProtection.rationale: Most easily violated constraint; foundational to MOQ integrity.
permittedReferences: Recognisable only after passing into static patterns
prohibitedReferences: DQ as mechanism through which a process operates
DQ as driver of adaptation, synthesis, or revision
DQ as something that can be 'applied', 'used', 'implemented', or 'accessed'
DQ as equivalent to creativity, exploration, or novelty as behaviours

levelDiscipline.rule: MOQ levels must not be collapsed into one another, but they interact continuously across the hierarchy.
specificConstraints: Stories, narratives, myths, and symbolic meaning are always social-level, never intellectual-level
Higher levels cannot originate lower-level patterns — they may modulate, formalise, or constrain them, but cannot bring them into existence as substrate
Intellectual analysis does not override physical, biological, or social realities — it operates within and on them
Social patterns do not produce intellectual truth; intellectual patterns do not produce social cohesion — but each can support or degrade the other through legitimate cross-level interaction
Reductionism across levels is prohibited: no level can be explained as merely a configuration of the level it depends on

canonProtection.rule: Canon status must be earned through explicit governance procedures.
specificConstraints: No silent edit of Canon meaning
Canon deprecation requires explicit marking; silent removal prohibited

descriptionVsPrescription.rule: Laws and Atlas entries describe how value patterns function structurally; they do not prescribe what individuals should do.
descriptionVsPrescription.rationale: Prescriptive framing imports moral-level claims into structural-level analysis.

polemicalLevelFraming.rule: Laws and Atlas entries should describe levels and their relationships without polemical framing of one level against another.
polemicalLevelFraming.rationale: The MOQ levels operate in hierarchy with conditional precedence; they are not in opposition. Polemical framing imports a fight that does not belong in foundational descriptions.

vocabularyConventions.description: Required vocabulary and conventions for project content.

lawIdConvention.constraint: Law IDs must remain stable across edits. Renumbering is prohibited.

fileTypeStandard.rationale: Supports embedded diagrams and visuals; compatible with Starlight

linkStyle.prohibited: Relative paths that break if files move; raw URLs inside Canon content

circleRippleTheory.scope: Supplementary theory authored by Kim Roar Spørkel, applying within its stated scope only
circleRippleTheory.authority: Defers to ai-instructions.mdx and core governance documents on any conflict
elements: Value Node, Becoming Value Node, Ripple, Circle, Keychain
Value Field, Zone of Value Resonance
Priming, Reserves, Trust, Reciprocity, Power, Enforcement, Coercion

attribution.boundary: Pirsig provides the Metaphysics of Quality foundation. All metaphors, diagrams, terminology, and operational models beyond MOQ are authored by this project.
attribution.responsibility: Responsibility for everything beyond Pirsig's original philosophy belongs entirely to the project author.

modelMaintenance.description: Rules for maintaining this model itself.
modelMaintenance.stability: This model describes architecture, not instances. It changes only when the project's underlying conceptual structure shifts.
outOfScope: Specific law instances and their full text
Specific glossary entries and their definitions
Specific Atlas entries and their score profiles
Operational state of the project (which entries are Canon, Draft, etc.)
modelMaintenance.rationale: Mixing schema with instances couples architectural stability to operational activity in a way that obscures which is which. The model defines the project's grammar; instances live in the project's MDX files.
